title: Separatedness of a free finite quotient algebraic space
statement: Let $S$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme], in the universes of [def-weil-size-convention, def-weil-affine-spectrum]. Let $W$ be a scheme over $S$ which is separated in the absolute sense: its diagonal $W\to W\times_{\operatorname{Spec}\mathbf Z}W$ is a closed immersion [def-weil-closed-immersion]. Let $G$ be a finite abstract group acting on $W$ by scheme automorphisms over $S$. Write $G_T=\coprod_{g\in G}T$ for the constant group scheme on a test scheme $T$. Assume the action is free on all scheme tests: $G_S\times_SW\to W\times_SW$, $(g,w)\mapsto(gw,w)$, is a monomorphism, that is, injective on sections over every $S$-scheme $T$. Let $Q$ be the fppf sheafification on $(\mathit{Sch}/S)_{fppf}$ of the orbit presheaf $T\mapsto W(T)/G_T(T)$ [def-pc-fppf-site, def-weil-pbc-sheafification], and assume $Q$ is an algebraic space over $S$ [def-trf-algebraic-space]. Then $Q$ is separated in the absolute sense: regard $Q$ as the sheaf $T\mapsto\coprod_{\varphi:T\to S}Q(T\xrightarrow{\varphi}S)$ on schemes over $\operatorname{Spec}\mathbf Z$; its diagonal $Q\to Q\times_{\operatorname{Spec}\mathbf Z}Q$ is representable by closed immersions on every scheme test. In particular $Q\to S$ is separated [def-sfb-presheaf-map-separated-diagonal]: its diagonal $Q\to Q\times_SQ$ is representable by closed immersions on every $S$-scheme test. Neither an affine neighbourhood for each orbit, Noetherianity, nor invertibility of $|G|$ is assumed. For $S=\operatorname{Spec}\mathbf Z$ this is the plain absolute statement.

source.place: Tag 02Z4, lemma-quotient-finite-separated, part (2), absolute version (as invoked in the proof of Tag 072C), with the free quotient notation of Tag 02Z2, lemma-quotient; change of base to Spec Z as in Tag 03I4.

proof.text: Put $R=\coprod_{g\in G}W$, with $s(g,w)=gw$ and $t(g,w)=w$. On a test scheme $T$, $R(T)$ is $G_T(T)\times W(T)$: the first coordinate is a locally constant $G$-valued function, not necessarily a single element of $G$. The assumed monomorphism therefore identifies its image with precisely the orbit equivalence relation. Reflexivity, symmetry and transitivity follow from $1$, inversion and multiplication of these locally constant functions. On each open-and-closed component $W\subset R$, $t$ is the identity and $s$ is an automorphism; they are etale, as is checked locally on the source directly from the definition (an isomorphism is locally a ring isomorphism, hence flat, finitely presented and unramified). Thus $R\rightrightarrows W$ is an etale equivalence relation.

source.place: Tag 02Z2, lemma-quotient, construction of the action relation and its proof

proof.text: Apply [lem-trf-etale-relation-quotient] to this relation over $S$. Its presheaf quotient is exactly $T\mapsto W(T)/G_T(T)$ from the statement, so its sheaf quotient is the specified $Q$ (uniquely compatibly with the quotient maps). Consequently $q:W\to Q$ is representable, surjective and etale, and the canonical map $R\to W\times_QW$ is an isomorphism. This proves the precise kernel-pair identity needed below; algebraicity alone would not supply it.

Apply [lem-sfb-space-change-base-to-integers] with $S\to\operatorname{Spec}\mathbf Z$. Write $\overline Q=j_!Q$, with exactly the section formula in the statement. It is an algebraic space, $W\to\overline Q$ is still representable surjective etale, and preservation of fibre products identifies $W\times_{\overline Q}W$ with the same scheme $R$. Set $Z=W\times_{\operatorname{Spec}\mathbf Z}W$. The pullback of $\Delta_{\overline Q}$ along $(q,q):Z\to\overline Q\times\overline Q$ is therefore $j:R\to Z$, $j(g,w)=(gw,w)$: on a test scheme a point of this pullback is a pair with equal images under $q$. Since $\overline Q$ is algebraic, its diagonal is representable. Also $j$ is a monomorphism: equality of two pairs as absolute maps to $W$ forces their structure maps to $S$ to agree, after which the given relative monomorphism applies.

source.place: Tag 03I4, lemma-change-base-scheme, and Tag 02Z4, lemma-quotient-finite-separated, reduction to the relation morphism

proof.text: For $g\in G$ the component $j_g:W\to Z$, $w\mapsto(gw,w)$, is a closed immersion. Indeed the square with upper map $1_W:W\to W$, vertical maps $j_g$ and $\Delta_W$, and lower map $Z\to Z$, $(x,y)\mapsto(g^{-1}x,y)$, is Cartesian by the fibre-product universal property. The right vertical map is closed by the absolute separatedness hypothesis; [lem-weil-pbc-closed-immersion-base-change] applies. The closed images $A_g=j_g(W)$ are pairwise disjoint. If $A_g$ and $A_h$ shared a point for $g\ne h$, the residue-field point of the closed subscheme $j_g$ at that point would also factor through $j_h$ (its defining ideal is contained in the point prime). It would give two distinct $\operatorname{Spec}K$-points of $R$ with equal images in $Z$, contradicting the monomorphism from step 3.

source.place: Tag 02Z4, lemma-quotient-finite-separated, last two sentences; Tag 01QR, morphisms-lemma-base-change-closed-immersion

proof.text: The finite coproduct $j:R\to Z$ is itself a closed immersion, as follows explicitly without any affine-orbit hypothesis. Let $O_g=Z\setminus\bigcup_{h\ne g}A_h$ and $O_\emptyset=Z\setminus\bigcup_hA_h$. These are open because $G$ is finite, and cover $Z$ because the $A_g$ are pairwise disjoint. Over $O_g$ all components except $g$ are empty, so $j$ restricts to the base change of $j_g$, a closed immersion by [lem-weil-pbc-closed-immersion-base-change]. Over $O_\emptyset$ the source is empty and is a closed subscheme by the definition. Closed immersions are local on the target by clause (1) of [lem-weil-pbc-closed-finite-etale-zariski-local], hence $j$ is closed. This includes $W=\emptyset$ and the trivial group.

source.place: Tag 02Z4, lemma-quotient-finite-separated, finite coproduct of closed immersions with disjoint images

proof.text: Descend this closed immersion to the absolute diagonal using [lem-trf-space-closed-immersion-cover-descent] twice. First pull $\Delta_{\overline Q}$ back along $q\times1:W\times\overline Q\to\overline Q\times\overline Q$, obtaining the representable map $a:W\to W\times\overline Q$, $w\mapsto(w,q(w))$. In the cited descent statement take $Y=\overline Q$, $B=W\times\overline Q$, $b=\operatorname{pr}_2$, $E=W$, and the one-member etale cover $W\to\overline Q$. Then $B_i=W\times W=Z$, and $E_i=W\times_{\overline Q}W=R$; its map to $B_i$ is $j$ (possibly with the two coordinates interchanged). Every scheme test is closed by the base-change lemma. Thus $a$ is closed on every scheme test. Apply the descent statement again with $Y=\overline Q$, $B=\overline Q\times\overline Q$, $b=\operatorname{pr}_1$, $E=\overline Q$, and the same cover: its local map is just $a$, so $\Delta_{\overline Q}$ is closed on every scheme test. All fibre products used here exist by [lem-trf-space-fibre-products-etale-covers]; representability of the two maps being descended follows from representability of the diagonal and its base change. This proves the asserted absolute separatedness.

source.place: Tag 02Z4, lemma-quotient-finite-separated, first sentence of proof; Tag 03KD, lemma-descent-representable-transformations-property

proof.text: Finally $\Delta_{Q/S}$ is the pullback of $\Delta_{\overline Q/\operatorname{Spec}\mathbf Z}$ along $Q\times_SQ\to\overline Q\times_{\operatorname{Spec}\mathbf Z}\overline Q$: on each test the two diagonals both impose equality of the two maps to $Q$, and the former test already fixes their common map to $S$. The sheaf fibre-product universal property gives this Cartesian square. Its pullback to any scheme test is a base change of the closed immersion just proved, hence closed by [lem-weil-pbc-closed-immersion-base-change]. Thus $Q\to S$ is separated [def-sfb-presheaf-map-separated-diagonal], with $G=Q$ and $F=h_S$. No assumption about separatedness of $S$, or about characteristic, has been used.

source.place: Tag 02Z4, lemma-quotient-finite-separated, conclusion; Tag 03I4, lemma-change-base-scheme, absolute interpretation

lean.statement: theorem free_finite_space_quotient_separated {S : Scheme.{u}} (W : Over S) [W.left.IsSeparated] (G : Type v) [Group G] [Finite G] (a : G →* Aut W) [Mono (prod.lift (Sigma.desc (fun g : G ↦ (a g).hom)) (Sigma.desc (fun _ : G ↦ 𝟙 W)))] (Q : AlgebraicSpace S) (η : coequalizer (yoneda.map (Sigma.desc (fun g : G ↦ (a g).hom))) (yoneda.map (Sigma.desc (fun _ : G ↦ 𝟙 W))) ⟶ Q.obj.obj) (hη : ∀ F : Sheaf (Scheme.fppfTopology.over S) (Type u), Function.Bijective (fun f : Q.obj.obj ⟶ F.obj ↦ η ≫ f)) : (∀ (U V : Over S) (b : yoneda.obj U ⟶ Q.obj.obj) (c : yoneda.obj V ⟶ Q.obj.obj), ∃ (P : Over S) (p : P ⟶ U) (q : P ⟶ V), IsPullback (yoneda.map p) (yoneda.map q) b c ∧ IsClosedImmersion (prod.lift p.left q.left)) ∧ IsSeparatedPresheafMap (terminal.from Q.obj.obj)
lean.note: The action relation is the coproduct of copies of W in Over S; its coequalizer is the full orbit presheaf, including locally constant labels on disconnected tests. The specified universal arrow η is sheafification at this presheaf. The first conjunct is the equivalent absolute scheme-pair closed-immersion criterion (Stacks 0AHS), with the product in Scheme over Spec Z, not in Over S; the second uses the recorded relative separatedness predicate.
